Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- Failing test: isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet opens COMPRESS-379.jar, selects the entry "META-INF/maven/" (a directory), and asserts that isUnixSymlink() is false.
- Current bug report: “isUnixSymlink returns true for Zip entries with Unix permissions 177777.” The attached jar shows an entry with permissions 0177777 (octal), i.e., all type and permission bits set. zipinfo shows it as “?rwsrwsrwt … META-INF/maven/”, indicating invalid/unknown type due to conflicting type bits.

Code path:
- ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink():
  return (getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG;
- ZipArchiveEntry.getUnixMode():
  returns 0 unless platform == PLATFORM_UNIX; otherwise returns the upper 16 bits of externalAttributes.
- UnixStat constants:
  LINK_FLAG = 0120000 (symlink type bit)
  FILE_FLAG = 0100000 (regular file type bit)
  DIR_FLAG = 040000 (directory type bit)
  PERM_MASK = 07777 (permission bits)

What happens:
- For the problematic entry, getUnixMode() yields 0177777 (all bits set). The current isUnixSymlink() only checks whether the LINK_FLAG bit is set, not whether it is the only file type bit set.
- 0177777 & 0120000 == 0120000, so isUnixSymlink() returns true even though other type bits are also set (e.g., directory/file bits), making the entry invalid as a pure symlink.
- The test specifically expects isUnixSymlink() to be false if “more than one flag is set,” which aligns with the idea that a symlink should be recognized only when the file type bits exclusively indicate a symlink.

Root cause:
- isUnixSymlink() uses a “bit present” check rather than an “exact type” check. It should mask off the file type bits and compare them to LINK_FLAG, e.g., (mode & TYPE_MASK) == LINK_FLAG, where TYPE_MASK is the Unix file type mask (0170000). Because it doesn’t do this, entries with multiple type bits set (like 0177777) are incorrectly classified as symlinks.

Consequence:
- Entries with invalid or conflicting Unix mode flags (e.g., 0177777) cause isUnixSymlink() to return true when it should return false, leading to the failing test.
